character_facts: The central warrior is physically capable of carrying or recovering another armored body through ruins.
He performs funerary or memorial acts for both a friend and his wife.
He is motivated by loyalty, grief, and adherence to a martial code.
Konrath is dead by this point on the page.
Edna is already dead before the events shown here.
characters_present: Konrath, shown as a recovered or carried dead body
Edna, referenced in narration but not visibly present
continuity_links: This page refers back to Konrath's death, which happened earlier.
It also refers back to Edna's disintegration at the column, an earlier event revisited here emotionally.
The narration continues a larger lineage theme by invoking the warrior's father and master.
dialogue_meaning: The narration says the warrior deliberately went back to retrieve Konrath's body, presenting Konrath as loyal and worthy of honor.
It states that he then honored his wife Edna at the exact place where she was destroyed.
It connects his conduct to a warrior creed taught by his father and master: true valor is detached from both triumph and defeat.
locations: A shattered battlefield or ruin strewn with corpses and debris
The base of a tall column or tower
A monumental stair and damaged ornamental structure
lore_facts: Konrath was considered a loyal friend of the central warrior.
Edna's body was disintegrated at the base of a column.
The warrior follows teachings inherited from both his father and his master.
Those teachings include a principle that a valiant warrior thinks in terms beyond victory and defeat.
plot_events: The armored warrior returns south through the ruins to recover the body of his loyal companion, Konrath.
He reaches the base of a great column or tower associated with his wife Edna's death.
He kneels and pays a final tribute at the place where Edna's body was disintegrated.
The narration frames his actions as guided by his father's and master's teachings about warrior discipline.
uncertainties: The exact identity/name of the central armored warrior is not stated on this page.
It is unclear whether Konrath's body is fully carried, dragged, or otherwise supported in the opening panel.
The exact nature of the floating debris and the broader setting is not explained on this page alone.
visual_summary: An armored white-haired warrior moves through a devastated landscape filled with wreckage and floating stone slabs under an orange sky. He carries or supports the body of another armored figure, then crosses the ruins toward a tall column or tower. At the base of an ornate structure near the column, he kneels in mourning. The page emphasizes aftermath, burial or recovery, and solemn tribute after destruction.
